summary: Amifostine (Ethyol) is an organic thiophosphate cytoprotective prodrug, dephosphorylated by alkaline phosphatase to an active free thiol that scavenges reactive oxygen species and detoxifies reactive cisplatin metabolites, preferentially in normal tissue. It is indicated to reduce cumulative renal toxicity from repeated cisplatin in advanced ovarian cancer (910 mg/m2 IV before chemotherapy) and to reduce moderate-to-severe xerostomia from post-operative head and neck radiotherapy (200 mg/m2 IV before radiation). Hypotension, nausea/vomiting, hypocalcemia and severe cutaneous reactions are the principal hazards; patients must be hydrated, kept supine, and have blood pressure monitored during infusion. It must not be used where chemotherapy or definitive radiotherapy can produce cure or survival benefit, as it may protect tumor tissue.
indications: Reduction of cumulative renal toxicity associated with repeated administration of cisplatin in patients with advanced ovarian cancer

Reduction of the incidence of moderate to severe xerostomia in patients undergoing post-operative radiation treatment for head and neck cancer where the radiation port includes a substantial portion of the parotid glands

dosage.t: Once daily, before each chemotherapy cycle

admin: For intravenous infusion only; reconstitute per labeling and inspect for particulates
Verify adequate hydration and correct dehydration before infusion
Keep the patient in a supine position during the infusion
Administer antiemetics (dexamethasone 20 mg IV plus a 5-HT3 antagonist at the 910 mg/m2 dose) before infusion
Monitor blood pressure before, at least every 5 minutes during (910 mg/m2 dose), and after the infusion
Interrupt antihypertensive therapy 24 hours before administration if feasible
moa: Amifostine is a prodrug that is dephosphorylated by membrane-bound alkaline phosphatase to a pharmacologically active free thiol metabolite. This thiol binds and detoxifies reactive metabolites of cisplatin and scavenges reactive oxygen species generated by cisplatin or ionizing radiation. Selective protection of normal tissue is attributed to the higher capillary alkaline phosphatase activity, higher pH, and better vascularity of normal versus tumor tissue, leading to more rapid generation and cellular uptake of the active thiol in normal tissues.

relative: Hypotension or dehydration (do not administer until corrected)
Patients on antihypertensive therapy that cannot be stopped 24 hours before infusion
Settings where chemotherapy or definitive radiotherapy can produce cure or significant survival benefit (risk of tumor protection)
monitor: Blood pressure during and after infusion
Serum calcium in patients at risk of hypocalcemia

preg: Can cause fetal harm. Embryotoxic in pregnant rabbits at intravenous doses approximately 60% of the recommended human dose on a body-surface-area basis. No adequate human data. Advise pregnant women and females of reproductive potential of the risk to a fetus; when used with cisplatin, also refer to cisplatin pregnancy information.
lact: There are no data on the presence of amifostine in human milk. Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment; when used with cisplatin, also refer to cisplatin lactation information.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is defined for renal impairment in labeling; the drug is used to reduce cisplatin nephrotoxicity. Ensure adequate hydration before administration.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is defined for hepatic impairment.

major: Antihypertensive agents - additive hypotension; interrupt 24 hours before infusion if possible and monitor closely
moderate: Other drugs that cause or potentiate hypotension - additive blood-pressure lowering
Highly emetogenic chemotherapy - additive nausea/vomiting and fluid loss
minor: Drugs lowering serum calcium - additive hypocalcemia risk
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction reported; avoid dehydration.
interactions.diagnostics: May lower serum calcium; transient hypotension during infusion.

serious: Severe cutaneous reactions (including erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis)
rare: Renal failure, myocardial ischemia or infarction (reported post-marketing)
emergency: Anaphylaxis or angioedema with airway compromise

monitoring: Blood pressure before, during (every 5 min at 910 mg/m2), and after infusion
Serum calcium in patients at risk of hypocalcemia
Skin assessment before, during, and for weeks after treatment
counsel: This medicine is given by a drip before your chemotherapy or radiation to protect normal tissues
You will need to lie down during the infusion and have your blood pressure checked frequently
Tell the team immediately if you feel faint, dizzy, flushed, or develop a rash or blistering
Nausea and vomiting are common - anti-sickness medicine will be given beforehand
Drink fluids as advised to stay well hydrated before treatment
pk: Active free thiol generated rapidly after infusion (minutes)
Rapid; measurable thiol in tissues within 5-8 min
Distribution half-life under 1 min; elimination half-life approximately 8 min
Short - cleared rapidly; under 10% remains in plasma at 6 min
Store lyophilized powder at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); discard unused portion
pearls: Do NOT use where chemotherapy/radiotherapy is intended to cure or prolong survival - amifostine may also protect tumor tissue
Keep the patient supine and monitor blood pressure closely; transient hypotension is the dose-limiting toxicity
Aggressive antiemetic prophylaxis (dexamethasone + 5-HT3 antagonist) is required at the 910 mg/m2 dose
Watch for serious cutaneous reactions; discontinue for lesions outside the injection site/radiation port or on palms/soles
Ensure hydration and correct dehydration before dosing
missed: Not applicable for self-administration - amifostine is given by a clinician immediately before each chemotherapy or radiotherapy session. Timing relative to chemotherapy/radiation is critical; if a dose cannot be given before treatment, do not give it afterward.
overdose: The most likely symptom is hypotension; manage with infusion of normal saline and supportive measures with the patient supine. Higher single doses have caused anxiety and reversible urinary retention. There is no specific antidote.
